ctx.x: Oh, what I wanted to ask you was, did you do any parade work? Any parade work?

Well, see, I was in the man so much around that, see, when you come to the parade, I played a parade. I played a parade. I played a walk in high. Once I played a parade. Twice, two days, I played. I played with Paul Barbarin. Boy, and then people walking from nine o'clock that morning to six o'clock that evening. With the square deals. Man, no more parades. Then I played the Labor Day parade the next day. On Canal Street. I played from the river and Canal Street to Elf's Place. And that was all. Who's band was…
I used to play him, too. But that was enough parade work.

items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1972-06-16
items.q: The brothers have a drummer too. Yeah. Bobberin, Paul.

ctx.x: Who were the best musicians for good steady time? The best rhythm man, you know, for steady

time then? Well, I played with so many good drummers, man. Yeah. Boy, they got the little boy, you know Bobberin. Oh, yeah. Yeah, that was the one. That was the Sydney band. Boy, that was a hell of a drummer. Louie or Paul, or? Louie. Louie, yeah. The brothers have a drummer too. Yeah. Bobberin, Paul.
Well, Louie still sounds good, you know. He sounds like a professional drummer to me.
